schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE INSURANCE (
    PID INT,
    TIV_2015 NUMERIC,
    TIV_2016 NUMERIC,
    LAT NUMERIC,
    LON NUMERIC,
    PRIMARY KEY (PID),
    CHECK (TIV_2015 >= 0),
    CHECK (TIV_2016 >= 0)
);
q1: SELECT ROUND(SUM(TIV_2016),2) TIV_2016 FROM INSURANCE WHERE TIV_2015 IN (SELECT TIV_2015 FROM INSURANCE GROUP BY TIV_2015 HAVING COUNT(*)>1) AND (LAT,LON) IN (SELECT LAT,LON FROM INSURANCE GROUP BY LAT,LON HAVING COUNT(*)=1)
q2: WITH SAME_TIV_2015 AS (SELECT TIV_2015, COUNT(*) FROM INSURANCE GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(*) > 1), DIFF_LOC AS (SELECT LAT, LON, COUNT(*) FROM INSURANCE GROUP BY 1, 2 HAVING COUNT(*) = 1 ) SELECT SUM(TIV_2016) AS TIV_2016 FROM INSURANCE WHERE TIV_2015 IN (SELECT TIV_2015 FROM SAME_TIV_2015) AND CONCAT(LAT,',',LON) IN (SELECT CONCAT(LAT,',',LON) FROM DIFF_LOC)

counterexample: INSERT INTO INSURANCE (PID, TIV_2015, TIV_2016, LAT, LON) VALUES (1, 100, 100.005, 1, 2), (2, 100, 0, 3, 4);
explanation: Q1 uses ROUND(SUM(TIV_2016), 2) while Q2 uses SUM(TIV_2016) without rounding. This leads to different results when the sum has more than two decimal places.
